sections.html: Lepidocephalichthys guntea usually reaches 6-8 cm; only very rarely are larger specimens of up to 15 cm reported in the literature. Available size: 6-8 cm. Origin: India.

The animal has a huge distribution area over the north of India and the adjacent countries. Here it often has to live under conditions that can be survived only due to the ability to breathe atmospheric air.

The water temperature can lie between 16 and 30°C, the span that the fish also face in nature. Water chemistry, e.g. hardness and pH, is of almost no importance. Any tap water fit for human consumption is also suitable for keeping Lepidocephalichthys guntea.
The fish are completely peaceful towards conspecifics and all other species of fish. Plants are not affected, but should be well rooted, as the loaches dig a bit.

The sexes can be distinguished best by a view from above. Males look quite lean compared with the females and have comparatively larger pectoral fins. The coloration varies a lot, which led to numerous synonyms. It is not sex-specific or population-specific and also varies with mood.

No successful breeding is known, but it should not be very difficult. It is recommended to try to initiate a rainy season for breeding: after a period simulating the dry season (no water change for some weeks at high temperatures), make large water changes with cool (18°C) and soft water.

What the peppered corydoras (Corydoras paleatus) is for community tanks with South American fish, Lepidocephalichthys guntea can be for community tanks with Asian fish: a very hardy, nice bottom dweller that reliably feeds on leftover food of its tankmates.

Lexicon: Lepidocephalichthys means "fish that looks like a Lepidocephalus"; Lepidocephalus is another genus of loach. guntea comes from the vernacular name of the species in Bengal.
